correctness.rationale: Every fixed finite set of flat-edge constraints equals BX=0 for a signed incidence matrix. Fourier inversion of the fixed-N iid ball increments and a unique Fourier peak give the uniform local limit (2πλ)^(-k/2)/sqrt(det BB^T); its determinant is the product of run length plus one. At cubic scaling, nonadjacent k-tuples yield the Poisson factorial moments, while adjacent tuples are asymptotically negligible; first- and second-moment estimates prove the two sides. All quantifiers and ranges are explicit, and standard-library verify.py passed 345 finite checks. Finite checks are corroborating, not the proof.

value.rationale: Exact flat edges are a natural structural defect of a discrete histogram gradient. A sharp cubic threshold and spatial Poisson law describe when an ordered histogram becomes locally strictly nonflat, including the no-flat-edge probability and both directions of the transition. Uniform Fourier control under fixed-total sampling is the substantive technical component, not a numerical substitution or arbitrary slice.
